notes: §1985:VIII.4.5.3 SR1: "The storage area associated with identifier-1 and the record area associated with file-name-1 must not be the same storage area." KeyedIoBinder.BindRead (relative and indexed) binds INTO through MoveBinder.BindIntoPhrase, then StatementValidation.CheckIntoReceiver and CheckPhraseOperandIsNotRecordArea (RecordAreaRule.InForce: Year < 2023), decided by StorageSharing.IsRecordAreaOf. Probes (work-rd-09/ov q1-q7, a record with OCCURS 1 TO 8 DEPENDING ON): refused COBOL6827 in SEQUENTIAL, RANDOM and DYNAMIC access: INTO the record (the witness), INTO the offset-0 full-width group holding the ODO table, INTO another 01; accepted: INTO W-S (run: '03ABC', and 'IK2 23' on a missing key), INTO RDAT(RN) or RN, partial overlaps whose subscript the READ itself changes (undefined, outside the rule). NOT implemented for INTO RR(1:), a reference modification spanning the record (q4 compiles and runs), nor, by the same IsRecordAreaOf exclusion, a level-66 RENAMES of the whole record. kb/Work PB5412 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-read3/rd-09.json).

next.reason: 1985: "The storage area associated with identifier-1 and the record area associated with file-name-1 must not be the same storage area."; 2023: "14.6.10, Overlapping operands, and 14.9.25, MOVE statement, General rules, apply to any cases in which ... share any part". 1985 forbids the INTO item sharing storage with the record area. 2023 drops that ban: shared storage falls under the overlapping-operand and MOVE rules, so the result may be undefined.
